PRIXEL
plate & pieces

Everything the planner app needs to know about the physical kit: one 24 × 16 grid at 5 mm pitch, 34 silicone piece SKUs, and a 1 × 1 typeface. Measurements are the vendor's own, cross-checked against the shipped SVGs and the Illustrator template.

The setup plate

drawn to scale

Pieces push into the flat face; the plate snaps to the acrylic press on four corner magnets. Those magnet bosses eat three holes at each corner — 372 of 384 cells are usable. The composition below is built from real kit pieces, with PRIXEL set in PRIXEL Mono at one cell per character.

Showing the print — what comes off the paper.
Constraint 01

Every print is mirrored

What you lay out on the plate prints reversed. The app needs a design view and a mirrored build sheet, and the build sheet is the one you actually work from.

Constraint 02

Inventory is finite

A design is only buildable if it fits the counts below. Live "pieces remaining" per SKU is the thing a planner does that a paper grid cannot.

Constraint 03

Two plates, one registration

Both plates overlay through the clear press for multi-colour prints. Model colours as layers that share one grid, not as separate documents.

Constraint 04

The press rotates 45°

Turning the press on the paper reuses the same shapes off-axis. Worth supporting as a plate-level rotation rather than per-piece.

Piece catalogue

31 of 34 SKUs ship in the kit

Size labels are height × width in cells — a 1×4 is four cells wide and one tall. That ordering is verified against the viewBox of all 31 shipped SVGs, and it is the single easiest thing to get backwards. Colour is the physical sort-bin coding, so it doubles as the app's grouping key. Shapes below are the vendor's own vector art, drawn at true relative scale.

Notes for the build

before you write the data model

310 or 316?

The product page headline says 310 pieces; its own spec table sums to 316. Take 316 as the table truth and make every count user-editable — kits get lost pieces and bought expansions.

Corner cut-outs are unconfirmed

"Three holes in each corner" is the vendor's wording, and the plate photo reads as an L-triomino. Measure the real plate before locking the placement mask.

Vector art is free

All 31 shape SVGs are authored at width="5mm" with 14.1732 user units per cell. Scale by 5/14.1732 to work in millimetres. No redrawing.

Mono counts aren't published

324 physical characters against 123 codepoints means duplicates of the common letters, but the per-character breakdown isn't documented anywhere. Make it editable too.

Rotations multiply the catalogue

Most pieces are placed in four orientations and several are chiral, so the real placement vocabulary is far larger than 34. Store {sku, cell, rotation}, not a pre-rotated sprite per variant.

Line pieces print differently

Green line pieces need noticeably less pressure than solid shapes. Worth surfacing on a build sheet that mixes both — it is the vendor's top troubleshooting entry.
